commandListPage.description: The commands here helps you operate the voice access user interface, settings, help options and modes of voice access.

commands.description: Tell voice access it's time to listen.
Put voice access to sleep. You will need to wake voice access up again to use it.
Turn off the voice access microphone. To turn it back on, long press on the microphone button.

Open a list of all voice access commands which helps you as you are working with voice access to perform different tasks.
Access the voice access Settings on the top right corner of the voice access bar.

Switch to commands only mode. You won't be able to dictate text, you'll only be able to give commands.
Switch to dictation mode. You'll only be able to dictate text, not give commands.
Unless you make changes, this is the mode voice access automatically applies. You can use commands and dictate text (on editable fields).

commandListPage.description: Voice access offers number overlays which is a great way to interact with items on the screen if you are unsure of the name. There is also a grid overlay to help you accurately move your mouse pointer to any location on the screen.

commands.description: Numbers will appear on all of the interactive items on your screen. Then say these numbers to interact with specific items.

Numbers will appear on all of the interactive items on the app you mentioned.
Numbers will appear on all of the interactive items on the task bar.
Remove the numbered labels from the screen.

Remove the numbered labels from the screen.
Cancel can be used to dismiss both number overlays and grid overlays.
Click on the numbered item.
commands.parameters: Number corresponds to the numbered label when overlays are on the screen.

commands.description: In the case of number overlays, this command will click on the numbered item. In the case of the grid overlay, use the number on the grid to guide the mouse pointer to that location. The grid overlay will be redrawn at this point at the location of the mouse pointer.
A 3x3 grid is drawn on your screen. You can use the coordinates of the grid to move your mouse in a specific direction.
A 3x3 grid is drawn on the app you are working on. You can use the coordinates of the grid to move your mouse in a specific direction.
Remove grid overlay.

Once you activate the grid overlay on a multi-display setup, you can quickly switch focus to another display by using either the alphabet or nato-phonetic in your command. For example, you can say either "B" or "Bravo" to move the focus to the display with label "B".
commands.parameters: monitor corresponds to the label alphabet on your other displays upon invoking the grid

commands.description: Use multiple coordinates of the grid in one command to guide the on-screen pointer to the final location. You can use up to five instructions at once.

commands.description: Go back to the previous state of the grid.

The grid is automatically redrawn when an item is marked and you can use the grid to navigate to where you want to drop the item.

Mark the object you want to drag. Marking happens at the <number> of the current state of the grid.
The grid is automatically redrawn when an item is marked and you can use the grid to navigate to where you want to drop the item.
Drag a previously marked object to a new location. The default is that the item will be dragged to the centre of the current state of the grid. Mark an object first before using this command.

commandListPage.description: With voice access, you can use your keyboard with voice commands. This is a great way to use shortcuts in your favourite apps. You can press a single key or a combination of keys, press a key multiple times, or press and hold down keys. Voice access also offers different ways to control your mouse to click, move and drag your mouse pointer on your screen.

commands.description: Perform a left click at the location of the mouse pointer. To click on a specific on-screen item, use the command "click <item>".
Perform a right click at the location of the mouse pointer. To right click on a specific on-screen item, use the command "right click <item>".
Perform a double click at the location of the mouse pointer. To double click on a on-screen item, use the command "Double click <item>".
Perform a triple click at the location of the mouse pointer.
Press a key or key combination.
commands.parameters:
Where key1, key2 etc are keys on the keyboard. 
For the Backspace, Enter, Tab and Delete keys, you can also give just the key name as a command
